heroHeadline: Nexus Intelligence's AI Chest X-Ray Screening Passes 25,000 Scans in Africa; Cambridge Fine-Tunes AI Advisories for Wheat Disease Early Warning
heroSubtitle: Pretoria-based startup Nexus Intelligence disclosed on August 16 that its AI chest X-ray screening platform — built on a Google-licensed model — has processed more than 25,000 scans across roughly 40 health sites in South Africa, Côte d'Ivoire, Sierra Leone, Cameroon and Vietnam, flagging likely tuberculosis and other lung abnormalities in under a minute for clinics with few or no radiologists. Separately, University of Cambridge plant scientists announced on August 27 that they are fine-tuning a large language model on five years of expert-edited advisories to automate wheat disease risk summaries for the CIMMYT-led Disease Early Warning Advisory System (DEWAS), which already spans Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Kenya, Nepal, Pakistan, Tanzania, Zambia and Bhutan, aiming to speed rust and blast warnings to the tens of millions of smallholder farmers the network serves.
footerNote: Data sourced from peer-reviewed journals (NEJM AI, Nature, Science, The Lancet, npj Digital Medicine), UN agencies (WHO, FAO, WFP, UNESCO, ITU, UNU), and major technology research outlets. Impact claims require independent validation; contested figures are marked.
